title: Veal Cordon Bleu
description: Thin veal escalopes wrapped around smoked ham and Swiss cheese, crumbed and deep-fried to golden perfection. Served with a Dijon cream sauce.

ingredients.notes: Don't add too much all at once — you can't take it out once it's in.

youWillNeed.note: For egg wash — use 1 egg per 250ml full cream milk. Whisk well before using.
Crumbing — panko gives a lighter, crunchier crust.
For deep frying — use a high smoke point oil such as cottonseed, sunflower, canola, or peanut oil.

method.instruction: Pound veal escalopes thin between two sheets of plastic wrap until even.
Lay ham and Gruyère on one half of each escalope. Fold the veal over to encase the filling and press the edges firmly to seal.
Dust each parcel lightly with flour, dip in egg wash, and coat thoroughly with breadcrumbs. Press the crumbs on firmly.
Heat oil to 180°C. Deep-fry crumbed veal for 2–3 minutes until deep golden and cooked through. Drain on paper towels.
For the sauce: melt butter in a small saucepan over medium heat. Add diced onion and cook until softened, about 2–3 minutes.
Deglaze with white wine and reduce by half, about 1–2 minutes.
Add thickened cream and Dijon mustard. Stir and reduce for 2–3 minutes until the sauce coats the back of a spoon. Season with salt.
Plate the veal and serve the sauce alongside — not poured over — to preserve the crisp crumb.

notes.title: Sauce on the Side
notes.content: The Dijon cream sauce is served alongside rather than poured over the crumbed veal. This preserves the crisp texture of the crumb — pouring sauce over would soften it. No demi glace is used in this dish.

notes.title: Gruyère Choice
notes.content: Gruyère is the classic choice for Cordon Bleu — it melts smoothly without splitting or becoming greasy. Swiss cheese or Emmental can substitute.
